newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Ranariddh provoked own overthrow-Cambodia ministry.
newsitem.headline: Ranariddh provoked own overthrow-Cambodia ministry.

text.p: Cambodia's ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh provoked his own overthrow through a year-long "reckless strategy of provocation", the country's foreign ministry said.

In a statement obtained by Reuters on Thursday, the ministry said Ranariddh had destabilised Cambodia by openly criticising Second Prime Minister Hun Sen's political party, conducting secret negotiations with Khmer Rouge rebels, building up his armed forces and weapons stocks and forming a political alliance that included the Khmer Rouge.

"Although Prince Norodom Ranariddh and his associates claim to be victims of provocation, in fact, for the past year, they have embarked on a reckless strategy of provocation, which has only served to destabilise Cambodia," the ministry said in a white paper.
Ranariddh's royalist FUNCINPEC party had attempted to strengthen its faltering political position by creating a crisis in which Hun Sen would make a mistake that benefitted Ranariddh, it said.

"Prince Ranariddh's actions -- both the attempt to make legitimate the Khmer Rouge hardliners and use their forces to secretly infiltrate the armed forces and the capital of Phnom Penh -- struck at the very heart of the idea of a coalition government," the paper said.

Ranariddh was ousted by Hun Sen on Sunday as Hun Sen's men pushed royalists out of the capital after fierce fighting. Ranariddh, who left for France before the fighting started, has vowed to lead a resistance from both inside and outside the country.
